[cols="1,4,1,6", options="header"]
.Register Map
|===
| Address | Name | Access | Description
| 0x0 | INTR_STATE | RW a| -
| 0x4 | INTR_ENABLE | RW a| -
| 0x8 | INTR_TEST | W a| -
| 0xC | ALERT_TEST | W a| -
| 0x10 | CONTROL | RW a| -
| 0x14 | STATUS | R a| -
| 0x18 | CONFIGOPTS | RW a| -
| 0x1C | CSID | RW a| -
| 0x20 | COMMAND | W a| -
| 0x2C | ERROR_ENABLE | RW a| -
| 0x30 | ERROR_STATUS | RW a| -
| 0x34 | EVENT_ENABLE | RW a| -
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_STATE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1 | `SPI_EVENT` | R | 0x0 a| Event-related interrupts, see !!EVENT_ENABLE register for more
information.
| 0 | `ERROR` | RW | 0x0 a| Error-related interrupts, see !!ERROR_ENABLE register for more
information.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_ENABLE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1 | `SPI_EVENT` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.spi_event is set.
| 0 | `ERROR` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable interrupt when !!INTR_STATE.error is set.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.INTR_TEST Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:2 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 1 | `SPI_EVENT` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.spi_event to 1.
| 0 | `ERROR` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to force !!INTR_STATE.error to 1.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.ALERT_TEST Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:1 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 0 | `FATAL_FAULT` | W | 0x0 a| Write 1 to trigger one alert event of this kind.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CONTROL Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31 | `SPIEN` | RW | 0x0 a| Enables the SPI host.  On reset, this field is 0, meaning
that no transactions can proceed.
| 30 | `SW_RST` | RW | 0x0 a| Clears the internal state (not registers) to the reset state when set to 1,
including the FIFOs, the CDC's, the core state machine and the shift register.
In the current implementation, the CDC FIFOs are drained not reset.
Therefore software must confirm that both FIFO's empty before releasing
the IP from reset.
| 29 | `OUTPUT_EN` | RW | 0x0 a| Enable the SPI host output buffers for the sck, csb, and sd lines.  This allows
the SPI_HOST IP to connect to the same bus as other SPI controllers without
interference.
| 28:16 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 15:8 | `TX_WATERMARK` | RW | 0x0 a| If !!EVENT_ENABLE.TXWM is set, the IP will send
an interrupt when the depth of the TX FIFO drops below
TX_WATERMARK words (32b each).
| 7:0 | `RX_WATERMARK` | RW | 0x7F a| If !!EVENT_ENABLE.RXWM is set, the IP will send
an interrupt when the depth of the RX FIFO reaches
RX_WATERMARK words (32b each).
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.STATUS Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31 | `READY` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates the SPI host is ready to receive
commands. Writing to COMMAND when READY is low is
an error, and will trigger an interrupt.
| 30 | `ACTIVE` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates the SPI host is processing a previously
issued command.
| 29 | `TXFULL` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates that the transmit data fifo is full.
Any further writes to !!TXDATA will create an error interrupt.
| 28 | `TXEMPTY` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates that the transmit data fifo is empty.
| 27 | `TXSTALL` | R | 0x0 a| If high, signifies that an ongoing transaction has stalled
due to lack of data in the TX FIFO
| 26 | `TXWM` | R | 0x0 a| If high, the amount of data in the TX FIFO has fallen below the
level of !!CONTROL.TX_WATERMARK words (32b each).
| 25 | `RXFULL` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates that the receive fifo is full.  Any
ongoing transactions will stall until firmware reads some
data from !!RXDATA.
| 24 | `RXEMPTY` | R | 0x0 a| When high, indicates that the receive fifo is empty.
Any reads from RX FIFO will cause an error interrupt.
| 23 | `RXSTALL` | R | 0x0 a| If high, signifies that an ongoing transaction has stalled
due to lack of available space in the RX FIFO
| 22 | `BYTEORDER` | R | 0x0 a| The value of the ByteOrder parameter, provided so that firmware
can confirm proper IP configuration.
| 21 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 20 | `RXWM` | R | 0x0 a| If high, the number of 32-bits in the RX FIFO now exceeds the
!!CONTROL.RX_WATERMARK entries (32b each).
| 19:16 | `CMDQD` | R | 0x0 a| Command queue depth. Indicates how many unread 32-bit words are
currently in the command segment queue.
| 15:8 | `RXQD` | R | 0x0 a| Receive queue depth. Indicates how many unread 32-bit words are
currently in the RX FIFO.  When active, this result may an
underestimate due to synchronization delays.
| 7:0 | `TXQD` | R | 0x0 a| Transmit queue depth.
Indicates how many unsent 32-bit words are currently in the TX FIFO.
When active, this result may be an overestimate due to synchronization delays.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CONFIGOPTS Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31 | `CPOL` | RW | 0x0 a| The polarity of the sck clock signal.  When CPOL is 0,
sck is low when idle, and emits high pulses.   When CPOL
is 1, sck is high when idle, and emits a series of low
pulses.
| 30 | `CPHA` | RW | 0x0 a| The phase of the sck clock signal relative to the data. When
CPHA = 0, the data changes on the trailing edge of sck
and is typically sampled on the leading edge.  Conversely
if CPHA = 1 high, data lines change on the leading edge of
sck and are typically sampled on the trailing edge.
CPHA should be chosen to match the phase of the selected
device.  The sampling behavior is modified by the
!!CONFIGOPTS.FULLCYC bit.
| 29 | `FULLCYC` | RW | 0x0 a| Full cycle.  Modifies the CPHA sampling behaviour to allow
for longer device logic setup times.  Rather than sampling the SD
bus a half cycle after shifting out data, the data is sampled
a full cycle after shifting data out.  This means that if
CPHA = 0, data is shifted out on the trailing edge, and
sampled a full cycle later.  If CPHA = 1, data is shifted and
sampled with the trailing edge, also separated by a
full cycle.
| 28 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 27:24 | `CSNLEAD` | RW | 0x0 a| CS_N Leading Time.  Indicates the number of half sck cycles,
CSNLEAD+1, to leave between the falling edge of cs_n and
the first edge of sck.  Setting this register to zero
corresponds to the minimum delay of one-half sck cycle
| 23:20 | `CSNTRAIL` | RW | 0x0 a| CS_N Trailing Time.  Indicates the number of half sck cycles,
CSNTRAIL+1, to leave between last edge of sck and the rising
edge of cs_n. Setting this register to zero corresponds
to the minimum delay of one-half sck cycle.
| 19:16 | `CSNIDLE` | RW | 0x0 a| Minimum idle time between commands. Indicates the minimum
number of sck half-cycles to hold cs_n high between commands.
Setting this register to zero creates a minimally-wide CS_N-high
pulse of one-half sck cycle.
| 15:0 | `CLKDIV` | RW | 0x0 a| Core clock divider.  Slows down subsequent SPI transactions by a
factor of (CLKDIV+1) relative to the core clock frequency.  The
period of sck, T(sck) then becomes `2*(CLK_DIV+1)*T(core)`
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.CSID Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:0 | `CSID` | RW | 0x0 a| Chip Select ID
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.COMMAND Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:25 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 24:5 | `LEN` | W | 0x0 a| Segment Length.

For read or write segments, this field controls the
number of 1-byte bursts to transmit and or receive in
this command segment.  The number of cycles required
to send or received a byte will depend on !!COMMAND.SPEED.
For dummy segments, (!!COMMAND.DIRECTION == 0), this register
controls the number of dummy cycles to issue.
The number of bytes (or dummy cycles) in the segment will be
equal to !!COMMAND.LEN + 1.
| 4:3 | `DIRECTION` | W | 0x0 a| The direction for the following command: "0" = Dummy cycles
(no TX/RX). "1" = Rx only, "2" = Tx only, "3" = Bidirectional
Tx/Rx (Standard SPI mode only).
| 2:1 | `SPEED` | W | 0x0 a| The speed for this command segment: "0" = Standard SPI. "1" = Dual SPI.
"2"=Quad SPI,  "3": RESERVED.
| 0 | `CSAAT` | W | 0x0 a| **C**hip **S**elect **A**ctive **A**fter **T**ransaction.
If !!COMMAND.CSAAT = 0, the chip select line is raised immediately
at the end of the command segment.
If !!COMMAND.CSAAT = 1, the chip select line is left low at the
end of the current transaction segment.
This allows the creation of longer, more complete SPI transactions,
consisting of several separate segments for issuing instructions,
pausing for dummy cycles, and transmitting or receiving data from
the device.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.ERROR_ENABLE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:5 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 4 | `CSIDINVAL` | RW | 0x1 a| Invalid CSID: If this bit is set, the block sends an error interrupt whenever
a command is submitted, but CSID exceeds NumCS.
| 3 | `CMDINVAL` | RW | 0x1 a| Invalid Command Errors: If this bit is set, the block sends an
error interrupt whenever a command is sent with invalid values for
!!COMMAND.SPEED or !!COMMAND.DIRECTION.
| 2 | `UNDERFLOW` | RW | 0x1 a| Underflow Errors: If this bit is set, the block sends an
error interrupt whenever there is a read from !!RXDATA
but the RX FIFO is empty.
| 1 | `OVERFLOW` | RW | 0x1 a| Overflow Errors: If this bit is set, the block sends an
error interrupt whenever the TX FIFO overflows.
| 0 | `CMDBUSY` | RW | 0x1 a| Command Error: If this bit is set, the block sends an error
interrupt whenever a command is issued while busy (i.e. a 1 is
when !!STATUS.READY is not asserted.)
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.ERROR_STATUS Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:6 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 5 | `ACCESSINVAL` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates that TLUL attempted to write to TXDATA with no bytes enabled. Such
'zero byte' writes are not supported.
| 4 | `CSIDINVAL` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates a command was attempted with an invalid value for !!CSID.
| 3 | `CMDINVAL` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates an invalid command segment, meaning either an invalid value of
!!COMMAND.SPEED or a request for bidirectional data transfer at dual or quad
speed
| 2 | `UNDERFLOW` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates that firmware has attempted to read from
!!RXDATA when the RX FIFO is empty.
| 1 | `OVERFLOW` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates that firmware has overflowed the TX FIFO
| 0 | `CMDBUSY` | RW | 0x0 a| Indicates a write to !!COMMAND when !!STATUS.READY = 0.
|===

[cols="1,3,1,1,6", options="header"]
.EVENT_ENABLE Register
|===
| Bits | Field | Access | Reset | Description
| 31:6 | `Reserved` | - | - a| Reserved
| 5 | `IDLE` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever !!STATUS.ACTIVE
goes low
| 4 | `READY` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever !!STATUS.READY
goes high
| 3 | `TXWM` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever the number of 32-bit words in
the TX FIFO is less than !!CONTROL.TX_WATERMARK.  To prevent the
reassertion of this interrupt add more data to the TX FIFO, or
reduce !!CONTROL.TX_WATERMARK.
| 2 | `RXWM` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever the number of 32-bit words in
the RX FIFO is greater than !!CONTROL.RX_WATERMARK. To prevent the
reassertion of this interrupt, read more data from the RX FIFO, or
increase !!CONTROL.RX_WATERMARK.
| 1 | `TXEMPTY` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever !!STATUS.TXEMPTY
goes high
| 0 | `RXFULL` | RW | 0x0 a| Assert to send a spi_event interrupt whenever !!STATUS.RXFULL
goes high
|===
